## turnstile v0.14.0

This release adds tamper evidence to the journal and pins its detection boundary with a differential test matrix. Opting in chains every journal row with SHA-256 over canonical JSON, batches the chain into Merkle-rooted epochs, and publishes each epoch to independent anchor sinks so a rewritten journal can be distinguished from a real one — with `opencode-turnstile prov --verify` available offline anytime. Marker classification and chain verification picked up fixes along the way.

### New: journal tamper evidence (#312)

- **Per-record hash chain** — with `tamperEvidence.enabled` (default `false`; existing journals and consumers stay on the unchained row shape), every journal row carries `seq`, `prevHash`, and `hash` (SHA-256 over RFC 8785-style canonical JSON of `{prevHash, ts, payload}`).
- **Merkle epochs** — every `tamperEvidence.epochEntries` (default 512) data rows, a chained `chain-epoch` commit row carries the epoch's Merkle root and head.
- **Anchor sinks** — epoch refs publish fire-and-forget at task completion to independent stores in escalating trust domains: `session-state` (host, default), `git-note` and `commit-trailer` (repository), or an external `{plugin: "..."}` sink; an array publishes to all and verification reports the weakest vouching domain.
- **Verification** — `opencode-turnstile prov --verify` folds the chain across rotation generations, re-derives epoch roots, and cross-checks anchored refs (exit 0 intact, 1 broken/unanchored); `tamperEvidence.verifyOnSessionEnd` runs the same check once per session at idle and journals/toasts the verdict.
- Config surface (`tamperEvidence.enabled`, `.anchor`, `.epochEntries`, `.verifyOnSessionEnd`) mirrored in `examples/turnstile.example.json`, the schema, the README config table, and `docs/architecture.md` §"Tamper evidence".

### New: differential tamper-matrix harness (#312, #315)

- Integration harness (`tests/tamper-matrix.test.ts`) builds a captured honest journal through the real write path — with a rotation generation and a task-completion anchor — and pins nine mutation classes to expected `prov --verify` verdicts: local edits/deletes/inserts/reorders/forks fail at the chain fold; rewrite-all with a recomputed chain and truncate-and-continue ("recurring cleaner") fail only at the anchor check; the un-anchored tail is a deliberately documented blind spot.
- Behavior pins for the prov CLI env, the row-8 absent split, shared harness options, and exact fold reasons (#315).

## Fixed

- Marker results are classified from the regex capture group (#310) — surrounding text no longer leaks into classification.
- Chain verify hardened against restart, rotation, and multi-host edge cases (#312): monotonic epoch indices across rotations and trust-root handling for pruned generations.

## Docs

- Replay global re-slice inclusion and boot memory bounds documented (#302).
- `freshFlags()` JSDoc covers counter fields (#304); waiver-unreachability test pin for `waiverStateNote` (#303).
- README compatibility matrix row updated to turnstile 0.14.x; `HOST_COMPAT` unchanged (floor stays OpenCode ≥ 2.0.22, < 3.0.0).

### Install

```
npx opencode-turnstile@0.14.0 init
```

## turnstile v0.13.0

This release makes the pipeline's front door configurable and turns the decision ledger into a queryable analysis surface. A new optional requirements phase can run before the planner, the decision ledger now captures human waivers and permission overrides (not just prompts and denials), and a new `prov-views` CLI derives origin labels, noise rates, and taste-drift aggregates from the raw ledger offline. Enforcement also picked up a fix: reviewer dispatches admitted through a dormant path now count toward the review ensemble.

### New: optional requirements phase (#306)

- **Config-gated** — `requirementsPhase` (default `false`) inserts a requirements agent leg before the planner; `maxRequirementsRounds` caps the loop, with waiver exemption, mirrored in the example config, schema, and `agents/requirements.md`.
- The pipeline-status formatter renders the requirements stage, and the policy injection describes the phase only when it is on.

### New: decision-ledger derivations (#290, #298, #289, #288)

- **`opencode-turnstile prov-views`** — derived views over the ledger: origin labels for stated prompts (instruction vs chatter vs waiver-carried), chatter noise rate, and taste-drift aggregates over denials and overrides, bucketed per day and per session; `--json` support with a sha256 hash on stated rows.
- **`prov:override` capture** — parent write/edit after-surface journals overrides, with a child-write adjacency tracker attributing the override to the dispatch context; rendered in the `prov` surface.
- **`prov:waiver` capture** — plan-gate and reviewer-gate waiver sites journal `prov:waiver` rows.
- **`turnstile-prov-views` skill** — vendored alongside `turnstile-prov` for the new surface.

### New: differential characterization harness (#292)

- `scripts/differential.*` and a suite of behavior-pin tests pin gate messages, config, journal shapes, decision-ledger shapes, replay round-trips, and export shape against drift.

## Fixed

- Reviewer ensemble counted on the dormant dispatch admit path (#293) — dispatches admitted while the review gate was dormant now credit the ensemble count, closing a hole where a credited approval could land without the ensemble being satisfied.

## Changed

- All functions brought under the 30-line ceiling (#305).
- Docs audit fixes across `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/usage.md`, policy prose, and the d01–d05 diagrams (#287); hero banner decision-ledger chip sizing fixes.
- Host compatibility tested list adds OpenCode 2.2.7.

### Install

```
npx opencode-turnstile@0.13.0 init
```

## turnstile v0.12.0

This release adds the decision ledger: turnstile now records the human side of the pipeline — every prompt you give it and every permission denial you make — into a secret-redacted, observe-only journal you can query with a new `prov` command. Capture is dumb and derivation is offline: rows are verbatim (after mechanical redaction), never classified at write time, and never coupled to enforcement — no new gates, no state changes, replay-inert.

### New: decision ledger (#277)

- **Capture** — every admitted parent-session prompt journals a `prov:stated` entry (secret-redacted at write time, capped at 2000 chars with a `truncated` marker), and each human permission denial at the plan/landing/hands-on ask sites journals a `prov:denied` entry with the ask kind. Capture is gated on the new `decisionLedger.enabled` key (default `true`); `false` silences all `prov:*` journaling with no other behavior change.
- **`opencode-turnstile prov`** — new read-only CLI subcommand printing the ledger: every session interleaved, or one session by ID; `--json` for raw rows, `--tail <n>` to bound output.
- **Redaction** — a fixed pattern list (API keys, AWS access keys, bearer/authorization headers, GitHub tokens, key/token assignments, private-key blocks) replaces matches with `[REDACTED]` before truncation, so a secret straddling the cap boundary is never left half-visible.
- **Mechanics** — new pure modules `src/decision-ledger.ts` (entry builders) and `src/decision-ledger-redact.ts` (redaction); payloads are canonically serializable so a future tamper-evidence chain needs no migration of existing rows. `prov:*` entries are replay-inert and capture is fail-open (an error journals and never throws).

### New: hero/demo showcase (#278)

The README hero and demo SVGs now include the decision ledger in the rendered pipeline.

## Added

- `decisionLedger.enabled` config key (default `true`), mirrored in `examples/turnstile.example.json` and `schemas/turnstile.schema.json`.
- `opencode-turnstile prov [sessionID] [--json] [--tail <n>]` subcommand.

## Changed

- Docs, `d02-hooks` diagram, usage configuration table, and README updated for the ledger and the `prov` command.

### Install

```
npx opencode-turnstile@0.12.0 init
```

## turnstile v0.11.0

This release is about giving the operator a direct hand and tidying the engine room: a new opt-in gate lets you review a plan yourself before the plan-reviewer sees it, the skill surface is reworked around on/off control and evidence/config introspection, and a large refactor wave splits the enforcement core into focused single-concern modules with the architecture docs and diagrams synced alongside.

### New: opt-in user plan review (#269)

A new config gate pauses the pipeline before plan-reviewer dispatch so you can review the plan yourself first; your approval enters the gate flow directly. Opt-in via the plan-user-review setting; see `docs/usage.md` and `tests/plan-user-review.test.ts` for the enforced contract.

### New: skill surface rework (#263, #266)

- `turnstile-suspend` is replaced by `turnstile-on` and `turnstile-off` — suspension and resume are now two explicit skills instead of one.
- New `turnstile-evidence` and `turnstile-config` skills: publish/inspect evidence bundles and show the resolved configuration raw.
- `turnstile-status` and `turnstile-log` ship as skills instead of commands.
- `turnstile-setup` is renamed `turnstile-init` to match its npm run target.

### Fixed

- `fix(gates)`: shared retire helper; a rejected dispatch now clears the nudge latch (#271)
- `fix(install)`: the retired-path sweep removes repo-owned dangling symlinks and emptied directories (#265)
- `fix(config)`: boolean keys are terminal in scalar validation, so `true`/`false` no longer fall through string coercion (#268)

### Changed

- Docs: `turnstile-config` shows raw config contents in its report; `docs/usage.md` documents the retired-path sweep in install maintenance.

### Internal

- Module-split refactor wave: hooks core composed from module-level concern state, with extraction of dispatch/budget/review gates (#264), plan scan/status/enforce modules, ledger parent-edge registry, tool-policy guards, event stream handlers, permission evaluate arms, journal sinks, prompt admission, bash-write guards, config merge/validate, shell parsing, and verdict capture. Module map and d01/d02/d04 diagrams re-synced.

## turnstile v0.10.0

This release is about meeting the session where it is: the plugin now starts dormant until the pipeline actually engages, plans carry an impact advisory that replaces the blunt parent-hands-on block, bare subagent output gets a bounded marker-retry loop before it fails the gate, and the journal splits into per-session sinks so status, evidence, and the new `log session` timeline can reason about a session in isolation.

### New: dormant-until-engaged enforcement (#254)

The gates no longer fire from session start — enforcement activates when the pipeline engages (plan bound, dispatch made, or gate state present). `alwaysEnforce` opts back into always-on enforcement for setups that want the old behavior. New module `src/engagement.ts` owns the determination.

### New: plan-impact advisory (#256)

While a plan is bound, the parent's out-of-plan hands-on writes no longer block outright: the new plan-impact advisory classifies the write target against the plan scope (`src/plan-scope.ts`) and lets the hands-on ladder decide, with landing-gate preservation and relativized plan-impact targets (#247).

### New: marker-retry compliance loop (#251)

Bare subagent output that omits gate markers gets one bounded retry with the marker contract re-stated before the gate fails — instead of an immediate red gate on a formatting miss.

### New: `log session` timeline (#253)

`opencode-turnstile log session` renders a per-session timeline from the journal, with corrected credit folding, waiver counting, and rendering of policy/tool/permission/evidence rows and directory/reason/exempt-tool fields.

### Added

- **Per-session journal segmentation** — `journalPerSession` config key routes each parent session's journal rows to its own sink; replay merges per-session generations ts-ordered with the shared tail, and `status`/`evidence` read segmented sinks (#252, plus a replay fix to read session generations once with shared error handling).
- Commit-lint classifier gives a concrete mismatch diagnosis and escalates through a retry, and now requires the separator space its regex always demanded (#257).

### Changed

- Plan gate: write targets outside the project are classified uninspectable so the hands-on ladder decides, rather than the plan gate guessing (#258).

### Fixed

- `fix(commit-lint)`: classifier requires the separator space the regex requires (#248)
- `fix`: landing gate preserved and plan-impact targets relativized (#247)
- Docs: per-session persistence across usage/architecture/policy prose; d03/d04/d05 diagrams updated and re-rendered

### Security

- Dependency override: `minimatch` pinned to ^11.0.1 (CVE-2026-118764)

### Notes

Zero runtime dependencies, as always. Host compatibility: ≥2.0.22, <3.0.0. Full docs: [README](https://github.com/edseabolt/turnstile#readme), [usage](docs/usage.md), [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [SECURITY](SECURITY.md). Install pinned: `npx opencode-turnstile@0.10.0 …`.

PR evidence artifact: post verified gate summary as a sticky PR comment
Polish batch: fail-open journaling gaps, config validation edges, dead code, debuggability
Fix freshFlags() doc: it returns counter fields, not only boolean flags
Document the replay global re-slice inclusion bound in architecture docs
Refactor functions exceeding the 30-line size ceiling
